newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU probes Kyowa Hakko Kogyo, ADM.
newsitem.headline: EU probes Kyowa Hakko Kogyo, ADM.

text.p: Archer Daniels Midland Co (ADM) and Japan's Kyowa Hakko Kogyo Co are the only two companies being probed by the European Commission over allegations of price-fixing in amino-acids used in animal feed, a Commission spokesman said on Friday.
The spokesman said he "could not confirm" whether another Japanese company, Ajinimoto Co, was cooperating with the Commission in the investigation.

But he confirmed an article in the Wall Street Journal Europe which said that the surprise raids carried out by Commission inspectors on Wednesday and Thursday took place at ADM's offices in Kent, England, and Wiesbaden, Germany, and Kyowa's European headquarters in Duesseldorf in Germany.
The Commission announced on Thursday that it was probing a number of companies suspected of coordinating their pricing of amino-acids and particularly lysine, used as an additive in livestock feed.
But contrary to a report in the Financial Times on Friday the Commission was not probing any other U.S. companies besides ADM.

The Commission's investigation follows a decision last year by the U.S. Department of Justice to fine ADM a record $100 million after the agribusiness giant pleaded guilty of fixing prces of lysine and citric acid.
The Justice Department probe also resulted in charges against Ajinomoto and Kyowa Hakko Kogyo and Sewon America Inc.
The Commission can fine companies up to 10 percent of annual turnover for operating price-fixing or market-sharing cartels.
It confirmed last week that it was also probing Germany's SGL Carbon AG over allegations of similar criminal offences in the graphite electrode industry whose products are mainly used in steel.
Under EU rules, companies that may have been involved in cartels can cooperate with the Commission in return for fine immunity or a reduction in fines. -- Amelia Torres 322 2876841
